The test image shows tomato leaves with numerous small, dark (black/dark brown) spots scattered across the leaf surface, with some yellowing along the edges. The spots are tiny (1-2mm), irregularly distributed, and appear uniformly dark without lighter centers. This pattern is highly characteristic of Bacterial Speck of Tomato.

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image for Bacterial Speck shows dark spots on tomato leaves, similar in character to the test image. Both show small dark spots scattered on green tomato leaf tissue. The test image has numerous tiny (~1-2mm), uniformly dark spots covering the leaf — the classic "speckled" pattern of bacterial speck caused by *Pseudomonas syringae* pv. *tomato*. The yellowing along the leaf margin and the pinpoint dark lesions match well.
